newsitem.title: THAILAND: Marathon protesters reject Thai government deal.
newsitem.headline: Marathon protesters reject Thai government deal.

text.p: Thousands of Thai villagers camped outside Government House for three months demanding solutions to land and other disputes on Wednesday rejected a government proposal to end the protest and vowed to stay put.

After a stormy session on Tuesday, the cabinet agreed to compensate protesters who could prove they had lost land because of government infrastructure projects from a proposed two billion baht ($77 million) fund.
But the 15,000 protesters from the impoverished northeastern region, led by a social action group called the Assembly of the Poor, said the proposal was too vague.
"The Assembly of the Poor is not satisfied with the cabinet resolution because there is no clear time frame and action plan in it," the assembly said in a statement.
"Since our demands have still not been met we will continue to live here near Government House to press our demands."
The cabinet resolution was strongly opposed by some ministers because they considered the protest demands unreasonable.
Similar protests in the past have all ended in failure because of frequent changes in government.
